question: What is the colour of the flame when magnesium burns in air?
solution:
The correct answer is __**White**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When **magnesium** burns in air, it produces a **bright white flame**.
 
• This white flame is due to the formation of **magnesium oxide** (MgO).
 
• Magnesium has a high **affinity for oxygen**, leading to a highly exothermic reaction.
 
• The bright white light produced is so intense that it can cause **temporary blindness** if viewed directly.
 
• Because of this intense white light, magnesium is often used in **pyrotechnics** and **photographic flashbulbs**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Pink**__

 __
 
• **Pink** flames are not typically associated with the burning of metals like magnesium.
 
• In the context of flames, pink could be indicative of the presence of lithium compounds.
 
 
 
• **Green**__
 __
 
• **Green** flames are usually produced by the presence of **copper compounds**.
 
• For example, copper chloride can produce a green flame.
 
 
 
• **Red**__
 
 
• **Red** flames are often produced by the presence of **strontium compounds**.
 
• Strontium chloride is known to give a bright red flame.
